cleanIntro: Routine cleaning of a Bodyguard 38 takes nothing off the gun — cylinder out, bore and chambers, done. The Deep Clean path is Smith & Wesson's own five-point lubrication routine, which is the one place this book takes the cylinder and yoke out of the frame.

steps.title: Confirm this is the Bodyguard 38 book, not the J/K/L/N or X-Frame one
steps.action: Check that the revolver in front of you is an M&P Bodyguard 38. Smith & Wesson prints separate manuals for its J, K, L and N Frame revolvers and for the X-Frame revolvers, and neither of those books' contents apply here.
steps.prose: This matters more than usual on this model because its barrel is built differently from every other S&W revolver — the shroud and frame are one piece of material rather than a shroud keyed into a frame — so a procedure carried over from the J-frame book can be wrong in a way that damages the gun. The model number is stamped inside the yoke and readable only with the cylinder open.
steps.quote: There are separate manuals for S&W® J,K,L & N Frame Revolvers and the X-FRAME Revolvers - available free upon request or via download from our web site.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For M&P® Bodyguard®38 Revolvers — REV:M&P_BODYGUARD38-ALL_081225 — Cover page, p.1

steps.title: Trigger fully forward, then thumb piece forward and cylinder out
steps.action: Take your finger off the trigger entirely — the trigger has to be fully forward with no pressure on it before the cylinder will unlock. Then press the thumb piece forward, push the cylinder out to the left, and verify every charge hole is empty and the barrel clear of obstructions.
steps.prose: That first sentence is the Bodyguard 38's own quirk and it catches people: this is a fully enclosed-hammer double-action-only revolver with a long trigger, and resting a finger on it holds the cylinder locked. If the cylinder feels seized, look at your trigger finger before you look at the gun.
steps.quote: The trigger must be fully forward with no finger pressure on it to allow the cylinder to be unlocked and opened (FIGURE 15).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For M&P® Bodyguard®38 Revolvers — REV:M&P_BODYGUARD38-ALL_081225 — Unloading, p.21

steps.title: Muzzle up, extractor rod down, then look
steps.action: With the cylinder held out and the barrel pointing upward in a safe direction, press the extractor rod down and take out every cartridge or case. Then make a visual check that all charge holes are empty.
steps.prose: The extractor rod on this small five-shot is short, so it lifts the cases only a little way — with the muzzle down a case slides straight back into its hole and looks like an empty chamber. Muzzle up and one firm push clears all five together.
steps.quote: With the barrel pointing upward in a safe direction, press the extractor rod down and remove all cartridges or casings from the cylinder (FIGURE 17).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For M&P® Bodyguard®38 Revolvers — REV:M&P_BODYGUARD38-ALL_081225 — Unloading, p.21

steps.title: Nothing marked +P+ goes in this revolver
steps.action: Check the headstamps: +P+ ammunition must NOT be used in Smith & Wesson firearms. This is a lightweight alloy-framed .38 Special, so the temptation to reach for the hottest thing on the shelf is real and the answer is still no.
steps.prose: The manual's reasoning is that +P+ names no defined pressure limit — it is a loader's own marking, so two boxes wearing it can be far apart in what they actually generate. Standard .38 Special +P is a different matter and is what this revolver is rated for, but the marking on the box is the thing to read, not the price.
steps.caution: "Plus-P-Plus" (+P+) ammunition must NOT be used in Smith & Wesson firearms.
steps.quote: This marking on the ammunition designates that it exceeds established industry standards, but the designation does not represent defined pressure limits and therefore such ammunition may vary significantly as to the pressures generated and could be DANGEROUS.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For M&P® Bodyguard®38 Revolvers — REV:M&P_BODYGUARD38-ALL_081225 — Ammunition, +P+ paragraph, p.12

steps.title: If yours has the Crimson Trace laser, it is not Smith & Wesson's to warrant
steps.action: If your Bodyguard 38 is the model with the integrated laser, treat that unit as a separate product: it is covered exclusively by the third-party manufacturer's warranty and warranted solely by Crimson Trace Corporation, and claims about it go to Crimson Trace, not to Smith & Wesson.
steps.prose: Practically this decides who you call and where the gun goes when something stops working. Smith & Wesson also notes that firearms cannot be shipped to Crimson Trace Corporation, so a laser fault on a mounted unit is not solved by putting the whole revolver in a box to Oregon. It also means the laser's own documentation, not this manual, governs its battery and adjustment.
steps.quote: These accessories are covered exclusively by the third-party manufacturer's warranty. The Crimson Trace Laser is warranted solely by the Crimson Trace Corporation.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For M&P® Bodyguard®38 Revolvers — REV:M&P_BODYGUARD38-ALL_081225 — Crimson Trace Laser Warranty, p.42

steps.title: The barrel is not yours to remove
steps.action: Leave the barrel alone. On this model the barrel shroud and frame are one piece of material, and the stainless steel barrel tube inside it comes out only in a qualified gunsmith's hands using a special tool from Smith & Wesson, refitted with that same tool and a torque wrench.
steps.prose: This is printed under a heading reading FOR USE BY TRAINED GUNSMITHS ONLY, and the consequence is spelled out: a standard barrel wrench on this assembly destroys the shroud, and the shroud is the frame. Nothing about cleaning a Bodyguard 38 requires the barrel to come out.
steps.quote: The stainless steel barrel tube must only be removed by a qualified gunsmith using a special tool available from Smith & Wesson®. The barrel assembly is re-installed using the same tool and an accurate torque wrench.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For M&P® Bodyguard®38 Revolvers — REV:M&P_BODYGUARD38-ALL_081225 — Gunsmith Advisory, p.22

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: For routine cleaning that is the whole of it — an open, empty cylinder and nothing removed from the revolver. The bore, the five charge holes, the cylinder face and the frame window are all reachable from here. Deep Clean takes you through Smith & Wesson's own lubrication routine, which is where the trigger guard pin comes out and the cylinder and yoke leave the frame.
steps.prose: The manual bars going beyond what it prints, and what it prints is the lubrication sequence in Deep Clean and nothing further.
steps.quote: CAUTION: Never disassemble your revolver beyond the instructions in this manual.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For M&P® Bodyguard®38 Revolvers — REV:M&P_BODYGUARD38-ALL_081225 — Cleaning and Maintenance, p.23

deepSteps.title: Cylinder out — first two lubrication points
deepSteps.action: Push the thumb piece forward to release the cylinder and tip it to the left out of the frame, then put a single drop of firearm lubricant on the two points the manual marks as arrows 1 and 2.
deepSteps.prose: One drop means one drop. Excess lubricant on a small revolver collects unburned powder and residue into a paste that binds the yoke and the rebound slide, and this gun's whole enclosed-hammer mechanism is behind a sideplate you are not opening — so anything you flood in there stays in there.
deepSteps.quote: Push the thumb piece forward to release the cylinder and then tip the cylinder to the left, out of the frame. Apply a drop of firearm lubricant to the #1 points called out by arrows #1 and #2
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For M&P® Bodyguard®38 Revolvers — REV:M&P_BODYGUARD38-ALL_081225 — Lubrication, p.25

deepSteps.title: Drive out the front trigger guard retaining pin
deepSteps.action: Close the cylinder back into the frame, rest the frame on a non-marring surface with clearance underneath for the pin to drop out, and drive the front trigger guard retaining pin out with a 1/16 inch drift.
deepSteps.prose: The cylinder goes back in first because a closed cylinder is what supports the frame squarely while you drive the pin; doing it with the cylinder hanging open puts the load on the yoke. Use a proper 1/16 inch drift — a punch that is too small mushrooms the pin end and a screwdriver blade marks the frame, and you need clearance beneath or the pin simply will not leave.
deepSteps.caution: Support the frame on a non-marring surface. Nothing here is driven against a bare vice or a benchtop.
deepSteps.quote: support the frame on a non-marring surface (allowing clearance for the pin to come out) and drive the front trigger guard retaining pin out with a 1/16˝ drift
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For M&P® Bodyguard®38 Revolvers — REV:M&P_BODYGUARD38-ALL_081225 — Lubrication, p.25

deepSteps.title: Trigger guard down, cylinder and yoke assembly forward and out
deepSteps.action: Tip the front of the trigger guard down slightly. Then push the thumb piece forward, tip the cylinder out to the left again, and draw the cylinder and yoke assembly forward and out of the frame as one unit.
deepSteps.prose: The dropped trigger guard is what unblocks the yoke's path — it is not being removed, only rotated down at the front, and it stays hanging on its rear pivot. The assembly comes forward along the yoke's axis; if it stops, the trigger guard has not dropped far enough rather than the yoke being stuck.
deepSteps.quote: Pull the cylinder / yoke assembly forward and out of the frame (FIGURE 23).
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For M&P® Bodyguard®38 Revolvers — REV:M&P_BODYGUARD38-ALL_081225 — Lubrication, p.26

deepSteps.title: Yoke out of the cylinder — points three and four
deepSteps.action: Pull the yoke forward out of the cylinder, then apply a single drop of lubricant to the two points the manual marks as arrows 3 and 4.
deepSteps.prose: This is the one moment you can reach the yoke barrel and the inside of the cylinder's centre bore, and it is where a Bodyguard 38 that has gone gritty in double action usually is. Clean both bearing surfaces before you oil them; a drop of oil over old carbon just makes a lapping compound.
deepSteps.quote: Pull the yoke forward out of the cylinder and apply a drop of firearm lubricant to the points called out by arrows #3 and #4 (FIGURE 24).
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For M&P® Bodyguard®38 Revolvers — REV:M&P_BODYGUARD38-ALL_081225 — Lubrication, p.26

deepSteps.title: Back together, then the fifth point at the ratchet drive hub
deepSteps.action: Reassemble the cylinder and yoke into the frame, tip the cylinder into the frame opening and lock it closed, tip the front of the trigger guard back up, and press the retaining pin fully home. Then open the cylinder once more and, with the thumb piece still held forward, put the fifth drop of lubricant on the recessed ratchet drive hub before releasing the thumb piece.
deepSteps.prose: The thumb piece has to stay pressed for that last drop because holding it forward is what pushes the centre pin out and exposes the recessed hub the extractor rides on — release it and the recess closes up. Confirm the retaining pin is flush on both sides before you call it done; a proud pin will foul a holster and can back out under recoil.
deepSteps.quote: With the thumb piece still pressed forward, apply a drop of firearm lubricant to the recessed ratchet drive hub called out by arrow #5
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For M&P® Bodyguard®38 Revolvers — REV:M&P_BODYGUARD38-ALL_081225 — Lubrication, p.27

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHARGE HOLES
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and the five charge holes with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Finish each with a dry cotton cloth patch to carry out residue and solvent
Clean the cylinder face and the underside of the extractor star
If you shoot .38 Special in a chamber that has seen only lead loads, brush the full chamber length — a fouling ring makes the next round hard to seat

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cleaning cloth
Remove all cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints from the outside surfaces
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning
Never use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents on this revolver
If the gun carries an integrated laser, keep solvent off the lens and the battery compartment and follow the accessory's own documentation

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Five points, one drop of firearm lubricant each — no more
Excess lubricant collects unburned powder and residue and can interfere with proper functioning of the revolver
Lightly coat the metal parts, internal and external, with a high quality gun oil after cleaning

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: For extended storage oil the bore, chambers and internal working mechanism, and coat the external mechanism and barrel with an anti-rust oil
Do not store the revolver in leather or heavy cloth, and never with a plug in the barrel
Clean it again before use after storage
Check for signs of wear every time you clean it; if wear is noted, do not use the revolver

reassembly: Reassemble the cylinder and yoke assembly back into the frame, tip the cylinder into the frame opening and lock it in the closed position.
Tip the front end of the trigger guard up into position, then reinsert the trigger guard retaining pin and press it fully home so it sits flush on both sides.
Open the cylinder, hold the thumb piece forward and place the fifth drop of lubricant on the recessed ratchet drive hub, then release the thumb piece.
Close the cylinder and check for proper function of the revolver.
fncheck: With all five charge holes confirmed empty and the barrel clear, close the cylinder and confirm it latches. Take your finger fully off the trigger and check the thumb piece releases the cylinder cleanly — if it will not, you still have pressure on the trigger. Then cycle the double action several times pointed in a safe direction, confirming the cylinder indexes and locks at every stop and the trigger returns fully forward on its own, and check that the trigger guard retaining pin is flush on both sides of the frame.
